doc.title: Joe Wilder Part 1 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996

title: Touring Russia with Benny Goodman
summary: On the State Department trip the band got on well despite Goodman, and he felt Cold War tension and suspicion among the people.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: That’s great. Benny Goodman? You traveled with Goodman some?

Yeah. I went to Russia with Benny for the State Department. That was an interesting trip. It was a good orchestra, a really good orchestra. And had Benny been nicer on the trip I think we would have all had a wonderful time. But the guys in the band were so fond of each other that it just took the curse off anything else that was unpleasant you know. That was an interesting trip, very interesting. You could, the Cold War was at its peak, and you could just feel the tension, especially in Moscow and Leningrad, where you had a lot of military people, and it was just like a very eerie kind of a feeling, like at any moment you sort of felt that a war could break out. There was just a pall over everything there you know. And people were suspicious, they watched you, they just seemed to feel that anything, if you took a picture you were going to take a picture that would denigrate the people, and it was a little difficult. I don’t think any of us actually became close friends with anybody there because you couldn’t get that close to the people. They were afraid, and we had been warned to be careful you know.
Wow. To be so far from home.

And yet the people were just like people here, if you had removed them bodily from where they were and put them here, you would never have known that they were from Russia and I’m sure if we had done the same with us, they wouldn’t have seen the difference either you know. But it’s a psychological thing. It’s actually dangerous.
